Daily Digest Friday, July 24, 2026

HubSpot Launches Agent Hub, Only 18% See AI Revenue Impact, First Fully Agentic Ad Campaign

HubSpot centralizes AI agent management. HCLTech exposes the 90%/18% gap. Broadsign runs first fully agentic OOH campaign.

  1. 1

    HubSpot Launches Agent Hub & Agent Builder

    HubSpot expanded its Breeze AI platform with Agent Hub and Agent Builder — a centralized dashboard to deploy, monitor, and manage AI agents inside the CRM. Teams can now build custom agents using a low-code interface, connect them directly to CRM data, and set execution limits to manage costs. The shift: embedding agentic AI where customer data already lives, not bolting it on from outside.

    Read on MarTech ↗
  2. 2

    HCLTech: Only 18% of Enterprises See AI Revenue Impact

    The gap is stark: 90% of organizations say GenAI and Agentic AI are "transforming workflows," but only 18% report significant revenue impact. HCLTech's Blueprint for AI Leadership study found the difference comes down to integration depth — leaders embed AI into core business strategy and workflows, while followers chase efficiency gains that never scale. The 72-point gap is the defining challenge for CMOs right now.

    Read on Agile Brand Guide ↗
  3. 3

    Broadsign Executes First Fully Agentic OOH Campaign

    Broadsign's sell-side AI agent and Draft Digital's buy-side agent just ran the first end-to-end agentic out-of-home campaign — from audience targeting through creative approval to execution — without human handoffs. The agents used campaign goals to inform venue targeting, media selection, and creative workflow. This is the paradigm shift: media planning and buying compressed into agent-to-agent protocols.

    Read on Agile Brand Guide ↗
  4. 4

    Consumer AI Distrust? It's About Data, Not Technology

    New research from the Nuremberg Institute found that labeling content as "AI-generated" actually hurts performance — reducing trust and engagement. But here's the insight: the issue isn't the AI itself. Consumers care more about how brands collect, manage, and use their personal data. Transparency about data practices matters more than transparency about AI tools. The trust gap is a data governance problem wearing an AI mask.

  5. 5

    OpenAI Launches Health Features in ChatGPT

    OpenAI announced "Health in ChatGPT" — new product features aimed at health-related use cases. Details are still emerging, but this signals OpenAI's continued push into vertical applications beyond general-purpose chat. For marketers in health, wellness, and adjacent spaces: the platform you're building for just got new native capabilities. Read this one: The HCLTech study on the 90%/18% gap. Almost everyone's "transforming workflows" with AI. Almost no one's seeing revenue impact. The difference? Leaders aren't just using AI tools — they're rebuilding business processes around AI capabilities. That's the work most organizations are still avoiding.
